source: ICE Futures U.S. Rulebook, Chapter 9 Cocoa (Rules 9.00-9.27, Resolutions 1-4), read 2026-11-17; earlier values from ICE Submission 20-10 (Jan 14 2020) and Submission 24-137 (Sep 13 2024)
fnd_rule: 10 business days before the first business day of the delivery month; last notice day 10 business days before the last business day; deliveries from the 6th to the last business day
groups_note: Group A and C lists from Rule 9.18(b)(i) as read; Group B list as read (includes 'and others'); origins seen in ICE grading files but not named in the read text are put in Group B only where ICE's grading results show the $80 premium.
count_note: beans per kg: standard / maximum; a lot over its class maximum but within the next class is delivered at that class's premium; over 1,400 not deliverable; since the May 2020 contract the class is set by the count at grading (Submission 20-10)

defects.note: over these limits not deliverable; smoky or hammy cocoa not deliverable

waste.note: 1.01-2.50%: deduction = waste - 1.0; 2.51-5.00%: 1.5 + 1.5 x (waste - 2.5); deducted from invoice weight

port_note: Rule 9.02(c): no price differential by delivery point; seller chooses
certificate_validity: Rule 9.18(d)(ii): a certificate issued in a delivery period is valid for the rest of it and the next; issued outside a delivery period, for the next two delivery periods. Growth, condition, waste and count stay valid while the lot is identifiable; grade must be renewed. Expired lots may be re-graded (unlike coffee); lots that failed cannot be re-graded.
weight_loss_allowance: Rule 9.23(b): late or redelivered cocoa, 0.25% of weight per 30 days for most growths (separate schedule for Sanchez, Haiti, Jamaica)
customs: Resolution No. 1 (Apr 8 2025): cocoa submitted for grading must be customs cleared and free of duties, taxes and tariffs
load_out: Resolution No. 2 XI: 250 t/day (operator holding up to 30,000 t at a port) or 500 t/day; 60 days
eudr: None in the ICE Futures U.S. cocoa rules (US warehouses). ICE Futures Europe (London cocoa) has its own EUDR delivery rules; not modelled here.
lid_note: Living Income Differential set by Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana on forward sales from the 2020/21 crop; a physical premium, not an exchange rule (Bloomberg/Investing.com, 27 Jan 2020)
